stage1.name: Bounded cancellable replay preparation
plan: Keep source selection, archive128MiB/line512KiB/index512MiB/response120rows256KiB/cache2 limits and legacy compatibility unchanged.

Make index construction resumable. Each call consumes at most8MiB or20,000 input-line/parsed-row work units or75ms, checking cancellation between lines; time is a cooperative budget, not a hard syscall deadline. Reserve a maximum line/event allowance before a step to avoid exceeding hard byte/work bounds.
Hold global cache lock only for lookup/insert/eviction. Entry cancellation is atomic and release/eviction must not await a full scan. Dispose SQLite when the last in-flight reference returns.
Return state indexing with empty items and actual scanned/source-byte progress until EOF and commit. A failed or changed source invalidates its partial derived index, never the original archive.

Frontend shows concise existing-style spinner/progress. At most one outstanding page request, timer-driven continuation only while visible and non-private, pause on error with explicit retry; hidden/privacy/unmount discard late replies and stop scheduling.

During preparation, ignore per-second video rerenders but use latest playback position when continuing; readiness restores normal seek/follow/manual chronology without a second media clock or receiver.
acceptance: A synthetic archive requiring several slices returns indexing first, monotonic measured byte progress, then exactly the same complete rows/order/timing/dedup counts as a full read.
No partially indexed ready/empty result, no event loss/duplicate on chunk boundary; response and SQLite caps unchanged.
Close/release/eviction cancel in-progress entry without waiting for its build mutex and cannot publish that cancelled entry back to cache.
File identity/size/mtime or timing-anchor changes discard partial cache; hardlink/reparse/oversize checks remain effective.
Frontend continuation single-flight and timer-bounded; pause/privacy/unmount/provider switch/error prevent late requests or text disclosure. Explicit retry resumes correctly.
Seek during preparation uses latest time; small, empty, missing and unmapped archives keep existing behavior; loading controls do not displace buttons or rebuild video.
Lib-only compile/focused native tests plus focused frontend and full typecheck. Existing QA exe/hash untouched. Actual rebuilt desktop check remains separate.

receiverFailureCorrectionBeforeEdit.finding: live_chat receiver errors latch a session warning/preserve_source but do not mark the attached Archive failure_reason. A long watch-only YouTube source can hit its128MiB limit shortly after recording begins, leaving the much smaller recording archive marked complete. Actual known local receiver termination can therefore permit video-original cleanup despite missing later chat.

receiverFailureCorrectionBeforeEdit.plan: Latch terminal receiver failure in the existing session state and, under the same attachment mutex, mark any affected current archive interrupted without replacing a stronger existing typed write/cap failure. A later recording attachment to that already-failed chat session also cannot become complete. Cover spawn failure and panic paths as well as returned receiver error. Intentional clean stop and ordinary successful receiver completion remain distinct. Preserve the current ring/text, source-retention, durability-proof and video-finalization rules. No new receiver, retry or network action.

stage2BeforeEdit.decision: Implement writer, durable proof and bounded replay of versioned multipart archives together. Legacy single-file archives remain unchanged. The total128MiB text cap is not a requested truncation rule. Its replacement remains explicitly resource-bounded rather than claiming unlimited capture.
format: Version2 recording marker binds provider/job UUID/attachment UUID. Exact derived raw/events filenames, not caller or manifest-provided paths. Existing version1 proof/read paths stay compatible; a damaged version2 archive cannot fall back to legacy success.

Append-only bounded catalog records open/sealed parts. Publish each open record durably before accepting writes; sync the held part before appending and syncing its byte/line/hash seal. At most two active writer handles. No overwrite, resume-append, rename or truncate of another process source.

Close all accepted writes under attachment fencing, then verify/publish the detached catalog proof outside the shared live-chat mutex. Terminal status binds the exact catalog digest/count/bytes, not a large unbounded inline file list. Partial or unknown storage retains video originals and every chat part.

Crash replay reads only validated sealed contiguous prefixes and says partial. Unsealed/orphan/unknown files remain preserved; they are never silently adopted or removed. An absent terminal proof is never complete.

Use8MiB hard part bound (same as an existing preparation byte slice), rotate before a whole line would exceed it; raw line512KiB and normalized64KiB limits are unchanged. At most512parts across both streams,4GiB total and256KiB catalog. These are metadata/handle/disk resource limits, not proof that every8hour/high-traffic stream fits. Reaching a bound is explicit sticky partial, not a successful complete archive.

Keep existing1GiB free-space reserve; check before accepting more disk work. No unbounded in-memory chat or index. SQLite512MiB remains an independent explicit replay limit that cannot delete preserved source.

Replay exposes normalized parts as a virtual concatenated source; existing SQL global offsets and time/dedup ordering can remain. Hash each part during cancellable preparation; no ready/items/final totals before complete source-set verification. Hold opened read handles against writes/deletion until entry disposal, capped at512parts per entry and2actual index entries, including evicted in-flight owners.

Legacy frontend API and measured progress remain. No new UI, network reader, automatic retry, account access or data migration. YouTube producer temporary-source limit must be separately solved and tested; multipart recording alone does not claim that acquisition is fixed.

acceptance: Small injected part limits cross several boundaries without lost, split or duplicated rows; raw and normalized streams share budgets. Synthetic aggregate beyond128MiB is preserved/readable with bounded working memory; no real user archive fixture is rewritten.
Close-before-new-attach, receiver failure, cap/write/flush/catalog failure and panic cannot publish false complete. Partial video remains independently playable and originals remain protected.

Complete proof verifies every exact part and catalog; wrong identity, duplicate/gap sequence, length/hash corruption, malformed/oversized metadata and reparse/hardlinks fail closed. Unknown files remain untouched.
Crash at open/write/seal/terminal boundaries retains files and exposes only sealed verified history as partial; it cannot authorize cleanup or append into the interrupted source.

Replay multi-slice progress, cross-part seek/manual pagination, dedup/reorder, close/cancel, source identity replacement and2actualDB limits retain stage1 behavior. Do not concatenate entire archives into RAM or a new recording file.

plan: Derive a private validated chat descriptor from the already existing preflight metadata, bound to the exact video/channel and protocol youtube_live_chat. No second metadata/video receiver, account/cookie access or arbitrary info-JSON passthrough.

Build fresh<=8KiB input JSON with only fixed chat format/protocol/extractor/title and validated reconstructed canonical watch URL. Do not copy webpage_url/original_url/entries/formats/subtitles/headers/cookies/request data; no extractor fallback on chat failure.

Run the same pinned native chat downloader as primary format with --load-info-json - --format chat --output -, so stdout is continuous JSONL. No accumulating .live_chat.json source or whole-broadcast128MiB tail is needed. One callback feeds existing session ring and multipart writer; callback backpressure is bounded by pipes, not an unbounded queue.

Add narrowly scoped managed process streaming with<=8KiB stdin,16KiB reads,512KiB line bound and64KiB stderr. On stop/error/panic kill the contained child tree, drain/join actual worker threads before returning. A truncated last line is an error, not success.

Chat child only gets512MiB per-process memory guard plus100ms sampled32MiB owned temporary fragment and1GiB free-space watchdog. The observed disk threshold can overshoot between polls; do not advertise it as a byte-exact network or filesystem quota. Other media processes/limits remain unchanged. Existing24hour receiver lifetime is explicitly not an unlimited-recording claim.

Pass the existing recording cancellation into proof/finalization. No provider reconnect after a terminal failure, no deletion of failed/unverified sources, no app/Vite/example rebuild or automatic user interaction.
